task.title: How to Add a Photo to Outlook Signature?

user_message.content: is there a way to put my photo in my signature line in my outlook exchange imap?

status_update.description: Manus is working on your request

assistant_message.content:
Yes, you can add a photo to your Outlook email signature. The method varies slightly depending on which version of Outlook you are using, but the general process is straightforward.

---

## Adding a Photo to Your Outlook Email Signature

### Outlook Desktop App (Windows)

1. Open Outlook and go to **File → Options → Mail → Signatures**.
2. Select the signature you want to edit (or create a new one).
3. In the signature editor, place your cursor where you want the photo to appear.
4. Click the **image icon** (Insert Picture) in the editor toolbar.
5. Browse to your photo file and click **Insert**.
6. Resize the image as needed by clicking and dragging the corners.
7. Click **OK** to save.

---

### Outlook on the Web (OWA / Exchange Web Access)

1. Log in to your Outlook Web App.
2. Click the **gear icon (Settings)** in the top-right corner.
3. Search for **"Signature"** or go to **Mail → Compose and reply**.
4. In the signature editor, place your cursor where you want the photo.
5. Click the **Insert image** icon in the toolbar (it looks like a small picture).
6. Upload your photo from your computer or insert via URL.
7. Click **Save**.

---

### Outlook for Mac

1. Open Outlook and go to **Outlook → Preferences → Signatures**.
2. Select or create a signature.
3. Place your cursor in the signature body where you want the image.
4. Go to **Insert → Photo → Picture from File** (or simply drag and drop the image into the editor).
5. Resize as needed and save.

---

## Tips for Best Results

| Tip | Details |
|---|---|
| **File format** | Use JPG or PNG for best compatibility |
| **Image size** | Keep it small (e.g., 100×100 px for a headshot) to avoid large email sizes |
| **Hosting** | If the image doesn't display for recipients, consider hosting it online and inserting it via URL instead of embedding it |
| **IMAP note** | With IMAP accounts, the signature is managed locally in the Outlook app — it is not synced server-side, so you'll need to set it up on each device you use |

---

If you are using a **specific version** of Outlook (e.g., Outlook 365, Outlook 2019, Outlook 2016) or a particular platform (Windows, Mac, mobile), feel free to let me know and I can provide more tailored steps.

status_update.description: Manus is working on your request

assistant_message.content: Let me research the City of Plantation's requirements for both a Business Tax Receipt and a Vacation Rental Registration so I can give you accurate, step-by-step guidance.

Here is the complete guide for registering **101 Holly LLC** with the City of Plantation. The attached document covers both filings in detail.

---

## 1. Local Business Tax Receipt

All businesses operating in Plantation must have this. Here is the process:

**Step 1 — Prepare your paper application**
Download and complete the [Application for Local Business Tax Receipt](https://www.plantation.org/government/departments/city-clerk/local-business-tax-receipt). It must be 100% complete with a **wet ink signature and notary** before submission.

**Step 2 — Register on the Citizen Access Portal**
Go to [https://aca.plantation.org/CitizenAccess/default.aspx](https://aca.plantation.org/CitizenAccess/default.aspx) and create an account.

**Step 3 — Create the application record online**
- Start a New Application → Local Business Tax → Select record type (for a vacation rental, select "Vacation or Short Term Rental")
- Enter the property address, four contacts, and business tax information exactly as on the paper form
- Pay the **$15 application fee** online (+ $1 card processing fee)
- Upload the signed, notarized paper application

**Step 4 — City Review**
Monitor your email from `noreply@plantation.org` for any follow-up requests or invoices.

| Fee | Amount |
|---|---|
| Application Fee (online, card) | $15 + $1 |
| Code Compliance Inspection (if required) | $270 |
| Annual Business Tax Fee (most common range) | $105 – $210 |

---

## 2. Vacation Rental Registration

Since 101 Holly LLC is a non-hosted vacation rental (LLC-owned, no homestead exemption), you must complete all of the following:

**Documents to Gather Before Applying**

| # | Document | Notes for 101 Holly LLC |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Proof of Ownership | Print from Broward County Property Appraiser; provide Sunbiz record for the LLC |
| 2 | DBPR License | Apply at [myfloridalicense.com](https://www.myfloridalicense.com) |
| 3 | FL Dept. of Revenue | If Airbnb/VRBO collects sales tax, provide their DOR certificate + proof your address is registered |
| 4 | Broward County Tourist Development Tax | If platform collects it, provide their Broward County Tax Collector account evidence |
| 5 | Broward County Business Tax Receipt | Apply at [broward.org/RecordsTaxesTreasury](https://www.broward.org/RecordsTaxesTreasury) |
| 6 | City of Plantation Business Tax Receipt | See Section 1 above |
| 7 | Certificate of Insurance | Commercial liability: $1M per occurrence / $2M aggregate; City of Plantation as certificate holder |
| 8 | Interior Sketch | Hand-drawn floor plan with rooms labeled, closets, noise detector location, evacuation map |
| 9 | Exterior Sketch | Survey or aerial photo showing boundaries, pool, parking, noise detector |
| 10 | Sample Lease Agreement | Must include all mandatory terms per the Vacation Rental Ordinance |
| 11 | Affidavit of Compliance | Download from the City's website and complete |

**After Submitting**
Once the City reviews your complete application, you will receive an email to pay the Vacation Rental Registration Fee, Safety Inspection Fee, and Business Tax Fee. The property is then scheduled for a **safety inspection** before the registration is issued.

---

> **Important Note:** Incomplete applications will be rejected, and you will have **15 business days** to resubmit missing items. Operating without a valid Business Tax Receipt carries a **$250 fine**.

The attached Markdown document contains the full guide with all source links for your records.

status_update.description: Manus is working on your request

assistant_message.content:
That's a common situation and there is a clear path forward. Here are your options, from easiest to most involved:

---

### Option 1 — Contact the City Directly to Reset or Transfer the Account (Recommended)

The City of Plantation's portal does **not** support instant password resets — they explicitly state this on their website. You will need to contact them directly to either:
- Reset the account credentials to a new email, or
- Have them close the old account so you can register a fresh one under your email.

**Contact the Zoning / Business Tax Department:**
- **Phone:** (954) 797-2200
- **In person:** City Hall, 400 NW 73rd Avenue, Plantation, FL 33317
- **Office hours:** Monday–Friday, 8:00 AM – 5:00 PM
- **Email:** You can submit a message via the Contact Us page at [plantation.org/contact](https://www.plantation.org/government/contact-us)

When you call or visit, explain that:
> *"We have an existing account registered under a former employee's email address. We no longer have access to that email. We need to either reset the credentials or create a new account for our entity, 101 Holly LLC."*

They will likely ask you to verify ownership of the entity (e.g., Sunbiz registration, property ownership records) before making changes.

---

### Option 2 — Register a Brand New Account

If the City confirms there are no pending records or open applications tied to the old account, you can simply:
1. Go to [https://aca.plantation.org/CitizenAccess/default.aspx](https://aca.plantation.org/CitizenAccess/default.aspx)
2. Click **"Register"** in the top right
3. Create a new account under your current business email

> **Important:** Do this only after confirming with the City that the old account has no active records, to avoid duplicate applications or billing issues.

---

### Option 3 — Apply In Person

If the account issue is taking too long to resolve, you can bypass the portal entirely and submit the paper application **in person** at City Hall. The paper application still requires a wet ink signature and notary, so you would need that ready. In-person submissions go directly to the Zoning Department.

---

### My Recommendation

**Call (954) 797-2200 first thing** and ask for the Zoning or Local Business Tax department. This is the fastest path — they deal with this situation regularly and can typically resolve it in one call or visit. Once you have access to a working account, I can jump right back in and walk you through the application step by step.
